articleTitle: Performance comparison of ATSC 8-VSB and DVB-T COFDM transmission systems for digital television terrestrial broadcasting
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper compares the performances of ATSC 8-VSB and DVB-T COFDM transmission systems for digital television terrestrial broadcasting. The comparison is based on laboratory test results. The methodologies used for the laboratory measurements are analyzed. The possible network structure and implementation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Video and audio applications in vehicles enabled by networked systems
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A system architecture is proposed which enables information, communication and entertainment applications in cars, based on optical networking. Video and audio signals are transmitted as MPEG bitstreams. DVD and TV can be viewed on multiple color LCD screens.

articleTitle: A calculation-efficient algorithm for decision feedback equalizers
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We describe a method for decision feedback equalizers used in high speed digital receiver demodulators such as terrestrial digital television (DTV) receivers. The new algorithm uses the sparse channel characteristics of the DTV transmission. A variation of the decision feedback equalizer, namely the partial feedback equalizer, is also introduced. The sparseness of the channel is combined with the partial feedback equalizer to develop the new algorithm. Similarity with subspace based filtering is noted, which results in robust performance in the presence of noise. The new algorithm has a superior convergence speed and lower steady state mean squared error, as compared to conventional approaches.

articleTitle: System on silicon-IC for motion compensated scan rate conversion, picture-in-picture processing, split screen applications and display processing
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: An IC for consumer electronics TV sets performing 100 Hz interlaced/60 Hz progressive scan rate conversion has been designed. Picture-in-picture, split screen and picture improvement capabilities are also integrated. It applies a motion-compensating algorithm for high-quality scan rate conversion. PIP processing is done using a full frame based scan rate conversion method. Split screen applications with two asynchronous input sources are supported. All field memories are included using a high performance embedded DRAM technology. Therefore the IC, which is compatible with current TV concepts, meets economical demands with increased functionality.

articleTitle: Effective peaking filter and its implementation on a programmable architecture
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Peaking filters enhance the sharpness impression in video images, but are often complex and have some image quality drawbacks. We propose a peaking filter that combines a simple structure with good image quality. Thanks to this simple structure, our proposal is a good candidate for software implementation on a programmable architecture. We evaluated the performance on a 32-bit and a 64-bit multimedia processor.

articleTitle: VLSI implementation considerations for turbo decoding using a low latency log-MAP
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The soft-output Viterbi (see IEEE J. Sel. Areas in Comm., vol.16, p.260-4, 1998) algorithm (SOVA) and the log-maximum a posterior probability (log-MAP) algorithm are commonly used in turbo decoding. We propose to modify the sliding window MAP-algorithm of Viterbi to reduce the computational delay even further. We compare the simulation performance of this low latency log-MAP algorithm with the sliding window log-MAP. We also estimate the VLSI implementation complexities of the SOVA, the log-MAP and the proposed low latency log-MAP.

articleTitle: A Viterbi decoder memory management system using forward traceback and all-path traceback
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Register exchange (RE) and traceback (TB) are the two known memory organization methods used by a Viterbi decoder. This paper describes a new traceback technique that utilizes a novel forward tracing algorithm, which can greatly cut down the latency at minimal hardware cost. The new technique is compared with the conventional traceback algorithm. As an example, the architecture design implementing this new traceback technique for a Grand Alliance HDTV Viterbi decoder is described. System level simulation verified the new traceback technique.

articleTitle: Digital transmission scheme for ISDB-T and reception characteristics of digital terrestrial television broadcasting system in Japan
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper introduces a transmission scheme for ISDB-T, and proposes a soft decision decoding technique for ISDB-T receivers to improve reception performance under multi-path distortion and interference from analog television signals.

articleTitle: A comparative review of digital image stabilising algorithms for mobile video communications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The paper presents image stabilisation algorithms in combination with low bit rate video codec techniques in a mobile video communication environment by analysing standalone as well as integrated processing methods.

articleTitle: Chip-set for video display of multimedia information
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a chip-set for digital video processing in a consumer television receiver. A key aspect of the chip-set is a high flexibility and programmability of multi-window features with multiple teletext pages, Internet pages and up to three live video windows. The chip-set consists of a microcontroller featuring pixel-based graphics, and a video processor containing a number of flexible co-processors for horizontal and vertical scaling, sharpness enhancement, adaptive temporal noise reduction, blending of graphics, mixing of multiple video streams and 100 Hz up-conversion.

articleTitle: A single chip digital TV LSI with a flexible 2D graphic processor utilizing an optimized memory architecture
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A single chip digital TV LSI including MPU, transport decoder, MPEG audio/video decoder, and graphic processor is described. This LSI utilizes dedicated RISC processors and advanced unified memory architecture with special arbitration algorithm, which enables optimal memory access operation.

articleTitle: TCP: a next generation for TV control processing
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present a new 32-bit RISC integrated TV telecommunications and control processor (TCP) with bit-mapped graphics and all the necessary interfaces for use in high-end TV sets. This allows the implementation of complex user interfaces like WindowsCE(R).

articleTitle: Home gateway architecture for generic multimedia services
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Development of a prototype residential gateway based on low-cost off-the-shelf PC components is described. The goal is to show how such a gateway might operate to satisfy the requirements of a broad spectrum of customer requirements, from basic remote metering to full multimedia services. It features network enabled BIOS extensions or OS kernel extensions, which allow most of the gateway operating system modules and services to be loaded remotely from a head-server over a network link.

articleTitle: IC for motion compensated de-interlacing, noise reduction, and picture rate conversion
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: An IC for consumer television applies motion estimation and compensation for high-quality video format conversion. It achieves a perfect motion portrayal for all source material and many display formats.

articleTitle: New motion estimation algorithm for DV to MPEG1 compression domain conversion
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Motion estimation is one of the most time-consuming processes in an MPEG1 video encoder. In this paper, a novel hierarchical motion estimation algorithm for DV to MPEG1 conversion is presented. The algorithm performs a novel sparse search, and the block matching utilizes integral projection information from the compression domain. The algorithm has a much smaller computation complexity than those motion estimation algorithms currently available in the industry while maintaining comparable PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio).

articleTitle: MPEG-2 AAC coder on a fixed-point DSP
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an MPEG-2 advanced audio coding (AAC) coder on a fixed-point DSP. AAC is a powerful coding algorithm and offers high-quality multi-channel surround audio. We also discuss the implementation issue and effort in porting AAC algorithms to the DSP.

articleTitle: Perceptually tuned robust watermarking scheme for digital video using motion entropy masking
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present a watermarking scheme for digital videos that are based on human visual system characteristics. Our watermarking scheme inserts perceptually invisible watermark in the discrete cosine transform (DCT) domain. We have shown that the proposed scheme provides better results than two other popular schemes both in transparency and robustness.

articleTitle: Near-lossless embedded compression algorithm for cost reduction in DTV receivers
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present a novel near-lossless technique to reduce the memory costs of an MPEG-2 decoder with a factor of almost 6, by recompressing the I- and P-reference pictures prior to memory storage for motion compensation.

articleTitle: Video processing technique for multimedia HDTV with digital micro-mirror array
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Digital Light Processing/sup TM/ (DLP/sup TM/) technology is applied to a consumer multimedia HDTV prototype. The DLP/sup TM/ technology enables an all-digital display system that inputs the initial digital data, performs digital video processing and displays the processed data in digital form. No analog data conversion and processing are necessary from image creation to display. The result is bright, crisp images with visibly superior picture quality. This paper describes the architecture of the all-digital HDTV projection system and the video signal processing techniques from initial signal input to the final display on a 1280/spl times/720 Digital Micro-mirror Device/sup TM/(DMD/sup TM/).

articleTitle: Software decoding of HDTV
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We implemented a software decoder for HDTV MPEG-2 transport stream running on a standard processor with a multimedia instruction set. From the evaluation of the performance of this decoder it results that equivalent single processor of speed of about 1500-1800 MHz would be necessary to run the HDTV decoding entirely in software. This is confirmed by tests of the decoder with HDTV streams and with multi-threaded implementation of the decoder running on a multiprocessing workstation.

articleTitle: A method of de-interlacing with motion compensated interpolation
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: De-interlacing is an essential technology for the multi-format digital broadcasts and driving LCD/PDP. Motion compensation is useful for this, however, it has a risk for unsuitable interpolation. We propose new methods to solve the problems of motion compensation. These are "small blocks with wide motion estimation", "adaptive interpolation control by intra/inter difference" and "smooth motion switch". Finally, we measured de-interlacing performance by using re-conversion.

articleTitle: Region selectable auto-focusing system by digital PSF estimation
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A region-selectable fully digital auto-focusing system is proposed. After a region of interest is selected, the amount of out-of-focus in the region is estimated, and then the focused image is made by using a digital image restoration technique. If the selected region does not have valid step-edge, the system does not perform restoration. The proposed system can provide a convenient human interface for a digital auto-focusing system.

articleTitle: A fast bit allocation method for MPEG layer III
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The MPEG/audio layer III has been widely used to store the CD-quality music sequences. The layer III is an asymmetric codec in the sense that the complexity of the audio encoder is much higher than that of the decoder. A key task leading to the higher complexity is the bit allocation. The MPEG/audio layer III encoder has adopted schemes such as nonuniform quantization and Huffman coding to achieve high coding efficiency. However, all these schemes do not have the problem in quality and bit-rate controls. The usual method follows an iterative approach to perform bit allocation to achieve both quality and bit rate tuning. This method has immense complexity and will sacrifice the quality to fit bit rate. This paper presents an efficient allocation method, which has merits in both complexity and quality control.

articleTitle: 10-W single-chip class D power amplifier with very high efficiency for audio applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A one-chip integrated circuit (IC) of a 10-W class D audio power amplifier with very high efficiency using CMOS technology is presented in this paper. A mixture of a class D output stage and a bridge tied load (BTL) is the main topology of the proposed amplifier. This realizes a new 10-W IC audio power amplifier with a 12 V power supply with an efficiency of more than 90% and total harmonic distortion (THD) of 0.1% without any heat sink, all in CMOS and packaged in a normal DIP. The amplifier is implemented in a 4-/spl mu/m double-metal single-poly CMOS technology that supports MOSFETs that can endure the relatively high voltage of 12 V.

articleTitle: A low-power MPEG-2 codec LSI for consumer cameras
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have developed a low-power MPEG-2 codec LSI which has MPEG-2 encoding and decoding functions, high resolution still picture functions and a progressive frame encoding function. This LSI is specifically designed for realizing compact and low cost consumer cameras.

articleTitle: MPEG-4 visual texture coding: more than just compression
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The MPEG-4 visual texture coding (VTC) is a wavelet-based image coder that was created in the context of synthetic and natural hybrid coding (SNHC) to support applications that demand high-quality, efficient, and scalable textures. This paper provides an overview of various MPEG-4 VTC techniques and the functionalities supported by these techniques.

articleTitle: Fast MPEG-audio layer III algorithm for a 32-bit MCU
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: New implementation techniques for MPEG-audio layer III software by using a 32-bit MCU and DRAM are proposed. These make it possible to cut the processing speed requirement in half and realize real-time decoding.

articleTitle: Adaptive time-based location update scheme using fuzzy logic
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive time-based location update scheme that dynamically determines when to perform location update based on the moving distance of the mobile station and the incoming call arrival probability using fuzzy logic.

articleTitle: Wireless terrestrial interactive system based on DVB-T and SFDMA; the iTTi project
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the definition and prototyping of a terrestrial interactive system based on the DVB-T (digital video broadcasting terrestrial) standard for the broadcast channel (downstream) and the novel synchronous frequency division multiple access (SFDMA) technique for the return channel (upstream). The system has been conceived and implemented in the framework of the European ACTS iTTi project. The approach is to transmit bursts of low bit rate data from domestic DVB-T receivers back to the broadcaster within the UHF band. System specification, complete hardware prototyping and complexity estimation in view of VLSI implementation of the receiver has been carried out within the project.

articleTitle: Memory reduction by Haar wavelet transform for MPEG decoder
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In MPEG-2 HDTV, the bandwidth and memory size requirements are very large. We present a simple algorithm that requires low complexity hardware for the MPEG-2 decoder memory reduction. Our algorithm is based on the Haar wavelet transform (HWT), with no multipliers needed. Following the HWT, we use a variable-length coder to compress the data before storing them in the memory for future references. Our technique cuts down the memory requirement from 12 Mbytes to 7 Mbytes for the 4:2:0 HDTV application.

articleTitle: A quad-tree embedded compression algorithm for memory-saving DTV decoders
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes an efficient and simple algorithm to compress reference frames in DTV decoders for reducing memory and I/O bandwidth requirements. The proposed quad-tree embedded algorithm can efficiently compress each macro-block to a specified bit count exactly, which can be stored at fixed location for easy retrieval. It is shown that the proposed algorithm can compress reference frames up to a compression ratio of 8:1 without significant quality degradation.

articleTitle: A cost-effective D-TV system chip set
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper proposes a cost-effective D-TV system chip set. The video decoder is applicable up to MP@HL, and a new down-decode technique is adopted to reduce an amount of video frame memory to a quarter.

articleTitle: DSP-based real-time video decoding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper we describe the implementation of MPEG4/H.263 real-time video decoding on the high performance fixed-point DSP. This series of DSP utilize a common core based on VelociTI/sup TM/, the advanced very long instruction word (VLIW) DSP architecture, which makes them ideal for the high performance embedded multimedia applications. On the EVM board of this kind of DSP (CPU frequency 160 MHz) we were able to demonstrate decoding of MPEG-4/H.263 bitstream coded at 700 Kbps, CIF (352/spl times/288), at a speed of 55/65 fps, respectively. Applications such as consumer set-top boxes that decode streaming video on the Internet and packet-based videophones will benefit from this performance.

articleTitle: Hologram display model
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A so called hologram is a fully autostereoscopic 3D color display offering up to 128 depth level in front of and behind the display screen itself. These new display features will be achieved by an arrangement of lenticular glasses, color and brightness filters and a binary liquid crystal display being writable by laser beams and being erasable by electrical fields. The LC-layer can be substituted by a cheap image-coded black/white film showing a 3D-photo. A first model of a 20/spl times/16 inch 3D colour picture is presented.

articleTitle: A programmable DSP solution to a solid state audio player
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Portable solid state audio players are currently reaching consumers through the advent of new audio compression algorithms and non-volatile flash memory technology. This paper presents a low-power, software programmable portable audio system utilizing these technologies. The key to this system is a 16-bit, fixed point digital signal processor (DSP) that handles decoding and other features while allowing software upgradeability.

articleTitle: New rate control schemes for low bitrate video coding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A new rate control algorithm based on type selection procedures is proposed. Three type selection procedures are employed in this synthesis. The two bits prediction modes included in these procedures, i.e., variance-based and activity-based and activity-based prediction model, are also developed. In addition, a rate control scheme based on the stable buffer status is developed while comparable coding performance to the traditional linear rate control algorithm can be achieved.

articleTitle: PLL synthesizer with multi-programmable divider and multi-phase detector
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Dividers in PLL frequency synthesizers are reduced by half with multi-programmable dividers by introducing the (N+1/2) one. It has faster lock-up time and no drawbacks. A multi-phase detector for higher loop gain is also introduced.

articleTitle: Digital filter design for a PAL TV modulator
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper develops a multirate digital filter design for the vestigial sideband (VSB) modulator required in the analog TV transmission systems, like PAL. The design is based on a complex baseband VSB filter running at 13.5 MHz sampling rate, digital multirate techniques for increasing the sampling rate by the factor of 9, and a combination of multirate techniques and digital mixing to translate the signal to the 38.9 MHz IF picture carrier frequency.

articleTitle: An efficient host/co-processor solution for MPEG-4 audio composition
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient software host/co-processor architecture for the implementation of MPEG-4 audio composition. The proposed solution is based on a specific partition between general-purpose tasks and DSP-oriented functionality, thus achieving portability, efficient partitioning of the processing resources and memory management.

articleTitle: Multimedia system on a chip for set-top box applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The MAP VLIW processor architecture provides an integrated programmable solution for set-top box (STB) terminal manufacturers-enabling multiple media applications (e.g. MPEG2 decode of one channel, digital PIP on another) to operate simultaneously on one chip. Alternately one can operate a single high quality application, like down decoding of high-definition television (HDTV) to standard television (STV). STB designers can program these applications using their proprietary algorithms in a high-level language, enabling easy product differentiation (such as cost vs. features, picture/sound quality, etc.) in a market segment full of several fixed-function solutions. New applications or upgrades can be downloaded to the STB. We describe how typical STB applications are mapped to the MAP parallel processing architecture.

articleTitle: Development of standard platform for home network equipment
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We developed a platform for home network equipment consisting of a high performance CPU with a real-time operating system (RTOS) and peripheral function chips connected to the CPU bus. We implemented the serial bus protocol (SBP-2) software and an IP over 1394 protocol on this system.

articleTitle: A cost effective MPEG-2 HDTV system and video decoder IC with integrated down decoder, graphics and display processor
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A highly integrated second generation HDTV IC that supports MPEG-2, ATSC, BS4, and other standards is presented. It performs transport stream demultiplexing, video decoding, down conversion for 480I/P displays, display processing and 2D graphics. A full resolution output is provided for HDTV displays.

articleTitle: Transparent, dynamically configurable RF network suitable for home automation applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The design and implementation of a mobile low power RF network appliance to connect mobile intelligent nodes in one communication system is discussed. Its applicability can be found in a wide range of domains such as home automation, low speed Internet networking, data logging applications, surveillance equipment and many others. The system features self-configuring point to point routing making it particularly useful for home automation applications.

articleTitle: Synchronization and control of multi-threads for MPEG-4 video decoder
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The implementation of the MPEG-4 video decoder can have many approaches. Because of the multiple functionalities offered by the MPEG-4 video decoder, the use of a programmable chip could be a better solution for many applications. For practical reasons, a multiprocessor chip or, sometimes, multiple programmable chips are often preferred for implementation of the MPEG-4 video decoder. We discuss the partition of the MPEG-4 video decoder into multiple tasks and mapping these tasks to a multiprocessor architecture. The issues of inter-processor communication and control, and synchronization of multi-threads are also addressed.

articleTitle: A scalable video compression technique based on wavelet and MPEG coding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present a scalable coding scheme based on discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and MPEG coding. It has the advantages of reusing the MPEG hardware and software as well as relieving the hardware limitation on the image size.

articleTitle: Scalable video coding with fine granularity scalability
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Scalable video coding has been an interesting research topic for a long time. Temporal, spatial, and SNR scalabilities have been studied over the years. As network video applications are taking off, there is a great need for scalable video with fine granularity that the previous scalable coding schemes cannot satisfy. This paper presents the reference technique for fine granularity scalability in MPEG-4, which will satisfy the need of many network video applications.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of a pre-FFT equalizer design for DVB-T
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Conventional OFDM employs a guard interval to combat delay spread distortion of transmitted data. This reduces the efficiency of the OFDM transmission. The combined OFDM-equalization strategy described here employs an adaptive equalizer to combat delay spread distortion and thereby facilitates the use of very short guard intervals and thus a more efficient OFDM modulation scheme. The OFDM receiver and the equalizer are described and performance is simulated for transmission in a multipath radio environment. It is shown that the combined OFDM-equalization method offers improved bandwidth efficiency over the conventional method but performance is sensitive to additive noise.

articleTitle: Fast digital image stabilizer based on Gray-coded bit-plane matching
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A fast digital image stabilizer using the Gray-coded bit-plane matching is proposed which is robust to irregular conditions such as moving objects and intentional panning. Experimental results show that the proposed digital image stabilizer is a computationally efficient alternative to existing digital image stabilizing systems.

articleTitle: System on a chip for digital still camera
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have developed a system on a chip for DSC signal processing. This chip includes conventional three chips (32-bit RISC, camera signal processor, and JPEG). This combined chip realizes 1/3 the mounting area, 1/4 the power consumption, and short processing time.

articleTitle: Implementation of modulated lapped transform using programmable logic
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a hardware implementation of the modulated lapped transform (MLT) which is commonly used in audio and video compression applications. The MLT is formulated into the form that takes advantage of the embedded FFT in the programmable logic devices.

articleTitle: Local threshold and Boolean function based edge detection
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Localization of edge points in images is one of the most important starting steps in image processing. Many varied edge detection techniques have been proposed. Different edge detectors present distinct and different responses to the same image, showing different details. This work presents a new approach for edge detection. The actual gray level image is locally thresholded using the local mean value to make a binary image. The binary image is checked for edges by comparing with the known edge like patterns, utilizing Boolean algebra. This approach recognizes nearly all, real edges and edges due to noise. For removing edges due to noise, we adopt another approach. This time the actual image is globally thresholded by the variance value of the image. The two resulting images are logically ANDed to get the final edge map.

articleTitle: Video coding application design for next generation system-on-chip architectures
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Consumer electronics ICs grow ever more complex while at the same time rapidly evolving technologies and constantly shifting markets demand shortened design cycles. This paper describes the implementation of an HDTV decoder using a novel approach to system-on-chip (SOC) design developed to meet the demand for short time to market. The approach combines a complete definition of the application in a high-level object oriented language, an an advanced compilation system, and a configurable multiprocessor/VLIW platform.

articleTitle: An object-based video watermarking
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper deals with the watermarking problem for irregular shaped objects in video. Extracting the meaningful objects from video, we have implemented the watermarking using the SA-DCT (shape adaptive discrete cosine transform) and conventional rectangular based watermarking using various padding methods. The experimental results show that the SA-DCT method is superior to all other padding methods in terms of the robustness against the image deformations such as lossy compression, additive noise, filtering, and clipping.

articleTitle: An open DSP software architecture for multi-channel multi-decoder consumer audio/video solutions
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: An architecture which seamlessly integrates multiple audio decoders onto a single DSP is presented. A new concept in the form of an open software architecture is implemented which allows third party owned intellectual property in the form of specialized software modules to coexist as value-added post decoder processing phases. This modular software architecture maintains flexibility and adaptability for future decoder and post processing integration. The means by which this architecture supports post processing functions across decoders is the focus of this paper.

articleTitle: Transform-based watermarking for digital images and video
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A new approach to digital image signatures is proposed. The proposed approach has shown to be resistant to several kinds of image processing and the JPEG lossy compression. Moreover, the digital signatures can be extracted from the watermarked image without resorting to the original image.

articleTitle: IEEE 1394-cable's home digital network interface of choice
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The OpenCable set-top terminal will serve as the gateway to the cable network's programs and services, including support for digital SDTV and HDTV on cable. The OpenCable set-top initiative has selected the versatile IEEE 1394 high-performance serial bus as the bridge between the diversity of applications delivered to the cable set-top and consumer electronic devices such as television receivers. The set of requirements for the set-top to digital television (DTV) interface are described. The implementation of these requirements embodied in the OpenCable interface design are presented.

articleTitle: An evolutional scenario for home network and basic trial of IEEE 1394 home network
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Clarifying the evolutional scenario of the home network in multimedia era, the paper studies subjects for investigating the home network, e.g. home network architecture, gateway functions and wiring technologies. Finally, ATM over IEEE 1394 is described.

articleTitle: A space-time beamforming RAKE receiver for third generation wideband CDMA base stations
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Base station antenna arrays are a promising method for providing significant capacity increases for third generation cellular mobile radio systems. This paper presents a space-time receiver structure and evaluates a range of direction-of-arrival (DOA) algorithms, to assess the potential capacity gains from the employment of multiple receiver antennas for wideband code division multiple access (W-CDMA).

articleTitle: An MPEG-4 based software video phone tolerant of Internet packet loss
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The Internet has become the most popular network in spite of its weakness in real-time multimedia service provision. This paper describes how to enhance the quality of the real-time video service under the current Internet environments. It first investigates various factors related to the quality. It proposes efficient methods to minimize the impact of packet loss and jitter in the consideration of the requirements and limitations unique to software implementation of MPEG-4 video.

articleTitle: Multiresolution progressive image transmission using a 2/spl times/2 DCT
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We propose to use a 2/spl times/2 DCT for the multiresolution progressive image transmission of images with the spatial scalability. Since the 2/spl times/2 DCT has simple computations and insignificant image quality degradation compared to the other convolution-based wavelet filters, it can be used for real-time progressive transmission of images through the Internet.

articleTitle: MPEG-4 camera for use with Internet
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents an MPEG-4 camera, the first consumer-electronics product that uses the MPEG-4 video standard. The recorded video and audio can easily be transmitted over the Internet or be used as motion pictures contained in home pages.

articleTitle: Robust transmission of progressive JPEG image coding in wireless communications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present an error-robust progressive JPEG image compression scheme over wireless channels. It utilizes a resynchronization regulation technique to isolate erroneous blocks, and then corresponding error concealment techniques are applied to reduce the error damage.

articleTitle: A trellis decoder for HDTV
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The United States Advanced Television Systems Committee has created a standard for terrestrial broadcast of digital HDTV signals that specifies the transmittal of 12 separate, interleaved trellis encoded data streams. This paper describes an area-efficient, low-latency delay, single trellis decoder that decodes all 12 separate data streams and provides seamless transitions between the two different expected operating conditions-with and without NTSC co-channel interference.

articleTitle: Measurement and characterisation of distortions in the digital terrestrial television channel
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a measurement campaign for the development of suitable RF channel models for digital terrestrial television. These are necessary for the development of demodulator devices that are optimised for high performance at low cost, since the performance of synchronisation and equalisation subsystems are critically dependent on the distortions in the channel.

articleTitle: PC-based DTV architecture
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents the first PC-based DTV architecture using an industry standard PCI bus to transfer decoded video data from a DTV decoder to the graphics subsystem of a multimedia PC. The proposed architecture eliminates: 1) the need for a separate video port cable between a PC-based DTV decoder and a graphics controller, and 2) the need for a nonstandard graphics controller video port. This paper also presents a proprietary method to burst decoded DTV data over the PCI bus with no visible video artifacts due to bus latency or different video/graphics refresh rates. In normal operation, this architecture consumes only about 31% of the bandwidth of a 33 MHz 32-bit PCI bus.

articleTitle: ATSC data broadcast services: protocols, application signaling, buffer models, profiles and levels
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The ATSC T3 S13 Working Group on Data Broadcast Services is about to release its Version 1.0 specification. The purpose of the paper is to provide a description of the most important principles making up the specification. More specifically, four components are presented: a collection of uni-directional delivery protocols; a DSM-CC-based application signaling framework; an MPEG-2 transport buffer model and finally; a profile and level-based classification of data services. The functionality provided by each of these components is reviewed.

articleTitle: A middleware for improving utilization of wireless data telecommunication and its efficiency
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Mobile computing user sometimes feel the inconvenience that wireless data telecommunication is unstable and restricted to a narrow-band width. We have developed a middleware for wireless networks that compensates continuous data streams and reconnects automatically. We have confirmed the effectiveness of the middleware for continuous data compensation.

articleTitle: Picture enhancement in video and block-coded image sequences
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We propose a sharpness enhancement technique for video and decoded image sequences. A non-linear function generates a correction signal that is added to the luminance edges. Spatio-temporal information is used to enhance details, avoiding blocking artefacts and noise.

articleTitle: Image contrast enhancement based on the piecewise-linear approximation of CDF
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper, we present an image contrast enhancing method based on the piecewise linear approximation of the cumulative density function (CDF). Reduced hardware is required for CDF calculation, since the number of bins is greatly reduced thanks to this approximation. With the proposed method, various contrast enhancing effects can be implemented such as histogram equalization, partial or entire histogram modification.

articleTitle: Internet enabled digital photography
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The principles and concepts of Internet enabled digital photography are outlined. The design and implementation of an interface appliance to connect digital cameras to the Internet is described. In addition details are given of the server-side infrastructure required to support a range of network-oriented services.

articleTitle: A practical rate control algorithm for VBR MPEG-2 video transmission over ATM networks
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper, a new joint encoder and channel rate control algorithm is proposed for real-time variable bit-rate video transmission over ATM networks. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme obtains both performance improvement and consistent quality, as compared with the conventional ones.

articleTitle: A fully transparent high speed data broadcasting method for the PALplus TV standard
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A novel transmission method is described by which a fully transparent digital data channel is embedded within the PALplus TV signal. A data rate of 500 kbps for ancillary television and multimedia services is achievable.

articleTitle: A motion adaptive 3-D de-interlacing algorithm based on the brightness profile pattern difference
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A novel motion adaptive de-interlacing algorithm is described. The accuracy of motion detection between fields is significantly improved by difference calculation with the brightness profile pattern instead of the simple pixel differences. The performance of a pure spatial interpolation is also enhanced by a directional filtering combined with hierarchical rule based detection scheme. The proposed algorithm is successfully implemented in (H)DTV video display processor.

articleTitle: Robust error concealment algorithm for video decoder
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A new error concealment algorithm is proposed to repair damaged portions of the video in the receiver. The proposed genetic algorithm based on the mechanics of natural selection and the natural generic system performs better than those of previous works.

articleTitle: General quality maintenance module for motion picture watermarking
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel control module that can be incorporated in a wide range of digital watermarking systems and that controls system watermarking processes to preserve picture quality.

articleTitle: Performance of an advanced receiver chip for DVB-S and DSS
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A DVB-S and DSS compliant single-chip CMOS device for QPSK satellite digital TV reception has been developed. This paper presents the chip architecture and details on the performance under different channel conditions.

articleTitle: An FM subcarrier data broadcast system for bus transportation status
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: An application of data broadcasting is described which allows transmission of accurate status of public bus transportation for the benefit of commuters. The status can be displayed on bus station display boards or on personal receivers.

articleTitle: Symbol synchronization in DVB-T system in mobile environment
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper symbol synchronization in DVB-T system in mobile environment is investigated. We show the basic differences in symbol synchronization when the channel is not static but dynamic.

articleTitle: A private/public key watermarking technique robust to spatial scaling
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Digital watermarking is the technique which embeds the invisible signal including owner identification and copy control into multimedia data such as audio, video and images for copyright protection. In this paper, a new watermarking algorithm which embeds information of the copyright owner and copy control using a private/public key and is robust to spatial scaling such as converting the aspect ratio in a screen and resampling for a spatial scalable hierarchy is proposed.

articleTitle: CD playback using a monolithic confocal laser coupler with a confocal knife edge (CKE) structure
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We previously reported a monolithic optical pick-up based on confocal optics (Narui et al. 1998). Although the optical pick-up is very stable in principle for a lens displacement, we found some substantial problems in using the confocal optical system for detection of tracking-error (TE) signal. In this paper, we discuss the inherent characteristics of the TE signal using the confocal optical system, based on the results of numerical analysis and we also propose another monolithic optical pick-up which has an improved TE detection method. Using this novel optical pick-up, we demonstrate CD playback with a single-beam device for the first time. Jitter level achieved is 6.7 ns. Drastic improvement in DC offset against lens shift in the radial direction is also achieved compared with the conventional push-pull method. The new optical pick-up also demonstrates to be a substantially stable system.

articleTitle: Closed space RFI testing
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: An effective closed space RFI testing method has been developed at Thomson Product Analysis Laboratory to assure competitiveness of the new designs. The paper discusses testing philosophy as well as development considerations regarding procedure, presentation of the results and acceptance criteria.

articleTitle: A robust watermarking method for high quality image
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We propose a new image watermarking method for copyright protection. This method is a block based approach in the spatial domain. In addition to the perceptual invisibility and robustness, the image quality is also considered during the embedding procedure. Block activity is calculated to embed watermark. The watermark strength and the spread of the signal into a block are controlled by the block activity measurement. Experimental results show that the proposed method is suitable for the high quality image.

articleTitle: Block-based image processor for memory efficient MPEG video decoding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The block-based image processor, implemented in an HD MPEG-IC for memory reduction, is described. It provides dual compression modes and enables full decoding and display of all 18 ATSC video formats with only 64 or 32 Mbits memory.

articleTitle: DVD-RAM disc reproducing techniques for DVD-ROM drives
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have developed techniques to reproduce DVD-RAM discs at DVD-ROM drives. The key techniques are reduction of feedthrough in the focusing error signal, reduction of the push-pull signal offset and the half tracking jump function.

articleTitle: A new 8-16 channel coding for high density recording
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We propose a new 8-16 channel coding which increases the recording density in tape storage. It can also suppress the low-frequency components efficiently. The trial system can encode user data at up to 200 Mbps. We describe the code construction and the code parameters. We also report on the evaluation of the low-frequency content and a hardware configuration.

articleTitle: Low bit rate vocoder algorithm for videoconferencing and Internet phone
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper analyzes the dynamic sparse algebraic codebook used to model a residual signal and proposes a new algebraic codebook structure as well as a searching process with improved performance. This paper makes it possible to select various pulse amplitudes differently from the conventional method. In addition, two pulses can be selected on the same track and LP delay is minimized at the transient period. For speech quality on the telephone line, a 5.6 kbps speech coder using the proposed algorithm was equivalent to the 6.3 kbps MP-MLQ in the subjective speech quality test. However, speech degradation was caused a little compared with the MP-MLQ where MNRU Q=15 dB.

articleTitle: VSB receiver design in the aftermath of field testing
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Digital television (DTV) is currently being implemented in the United States (U.S.), with special emphasis on high definition television (HDTV). The Advanced Television System Committee (ATSC) standard has been selected as the new DTV standard in the U.S., which is based on the digital vestigial side band (VSB) transmission system. A brief overview of the digital VSB transmission system field-test performance from several U.S. cities is covered. VSB receiver design parameters are discussed as a result of the field tests performed by early adopter DTV broadcasters.

articleTitle: A converter between MHEG-5 and HTML 4.0
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper proposes a converter for conversion between the MHEG-5 and HTML4.0 formats, based on a comparison of these formats. The DAVIC has adopted MHEG-5 as its multimedia presentation format, while HTML is the standard multimedia presentation format of the World Wide Web on the Internet. As the Internet and TV converge, MHEG-5 content created for broadcast services will be reused on the Internet, and HTML content created for Internet services will be reused in broadcasting. In order to reuse the content in this way, conversion between HTML and MHEG-5 will be essential.

articleTitle: Video moire cancellation filter for high-resolution CRTs
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The appearance of moire limits the performance of high-resolution cathode ray tubes (CRTs). Until now, cancellation circuits have used a small alternating image shift (wobble) to disguise moire, but these circuits introduce other artefacts like flicker. We present a novel solution for suppressing video moire with a specific non-linear filter. Advantages include simple digital video signal processing and negligible degradation of the image quality, even in graphics with very fine detail.

articleTitle: Low-cost HD to SD video decoding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art low-cost DTV decoding scheme. This novel approach consists of a combination of down-scaling and embedded compression within the MPEG decoding loop, and can save both memory and memory bandwidth. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach efficiently preserves the quality of the output low resolution image.

articleTitle: Design and performance of synchronized DMT (SDMT) modems for VDSL
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a very high-speed digital subscriber line (VDSL) solution called synchronized discrete multi-tone (SDMT), which is a flexible, low-complexity time-division duplexed implementation of DMT that provides key desirable VDSL features. The measured performance results quantify the achievable ranges and data rates of a currently-available SDMT VDSL system.

articleTitle: A new efficient access protocol for integrating multimedia services in the home environment
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a new dynamically adaptable medium access method that can be applied to home networks in order to create a distributed environment for multimedia and data processing services. The method uses a mechanism that detects silent periods in voice transmissions and dynamically adapts the bandwidth allocation between isochronous and asynchronous traffic.

articleTitle: A digital vestigial-sideband (VSB) channel decoder IC for digital TV (DTV)
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes a second-generation integrated 8-VSB demodulator-decoder which can receive digital TV (DTV) signals that are formatted according to the ATSC standard. This IC presents significant improvements over the first generation for the reception of strongly impaired signals.

articleTitle: A highly flexible video up-converter chip
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes a video up-converter integrated circuit designed for high-quality TV, projection and multimedia displays. The chip uses broadcast quality digital processing techniques such as interpolation and filtering to perform real-time up-conversion of an input digital video stream. The number of frames per second, lines per frame, pixels per line and scan rate of the digital video stream produced by the chip are fully programmable.

articleTitle: Adaptive matching scan algorithm based on gradient magnitude for fast full search in motion estimation
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: To reduce an amount of computation of the full search algorithm in motion estimation for video coding, we propose a new and fast matching algorithm without any degradation of predicted images compared with the conventional full search algorithm. In this paper, we show that the block matching error is proportional to the image complexity of the reference block in the current frame. The computational reduction results from an adaptive matching scan algorithm according to the gradient magnitude of the reference block. Experimentally, we significantly reduce the computational load, while keeping same error performance as that of the full search.

articleTitle: Delivering object-based audio visual services
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Delivery of audio-visual objects differs from the traditional video on demand systems in the characteristics of the presentations delivered. Video on demand has mainly been about delivering MPEG-2 audio and video. In the case of object based presentations such as MPEG-4 presentations, the media data and the media composition data are transmitted to a client as separate streams, typically with different QoS requirements, in the same session. Furthermore, as the number of objects in a presentation can be quite large, the overhead required to manage the session is large. Interactivity makes this problem more complex as the resources required for a session will now depend on the user behavior, especially when user interaction with objects changes the number of objects in the scene either by adding or deleting objects. In this paper, we present our recent work on delivering audio-visual services based on MPEG-4. The issues covered include object-based audio-visual (MPEG-4) servers, object scheduling, object-to-object communications, and content creation.

articleTitle: A low-power single-chip MPEG2 (half-D1) video codec LSI for portable consumer-products applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes the newly developed a low-power low-cost, single-chip MPEG2 (half-D1) video codec LSI for portable consumer-products applications. This LSI could encode and decode at 27 MHz with a power consumption of 0.5 W at 1.8 V.

articleTitle: A video display processing platform for future TV concepts
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a generic video processing platform architecture enabling HW-SW partitioning with high flexibility and programmability. This modular concept is suitable for a large range of applications and features and is used for implementation of a TV platform. A key feature is to create SW programmability for video signal manipulation at the functional and system levels and give cost-effective HW support for pixel-based processing.

articleTitle: Variable grid size motion estimation using spatial transformations
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Conventional spatial transform based motion estimation algorithms are not practical because of heavy computational loads. In this paper, we proposed variable grid size motion estimation method, which is more efficient than conventional spatial transform based methods and gives better PSNR performance than the conventional block matching algorithm.

articleTitle: A single-chip HDTV A/V decoder for low-cost DTV receiver
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper, a single chip HDTV decoder is presented which drastically cuts down the cost of a HDTV receiver. The cost reduction is achieved by integration of system demux, down-converting video decoder, and multi-mode audio decoder. System designers can also benefit from the features of our decoder which requires only 4 Mbytes of SDRAM (synchronous DRAM) for decoding the HDTV signal and various system-level functions such as the IEEE 1394 bus interface, the I/sup 2/C bus controller and the on-chip clock recovery function.

articleTitle: IEEE1394 S200 infrared wireless adapter
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have demonstrated the world's first IEEE1394 S200 infrared (IR) wireless adapter and verified its operation. Our adapters enable us to communicate using low cost devices with sufficient eye-safety margin. Further, we have indicated a design approach to reach a transmission distance of 10 m while keeping an easy alignment property.

articleTitle: Time-varied pitch gain predictor for tracing amplitude-varied periodicity speech
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We proposed a time-varied prediction gain to achieve a better representation of speech periodicity than the traditional approach. Due to non-stationary variation of speech, the proposed long term predictor (LTP) can well trace the detailed fluctuation of speech amplitude in both transient and stationary periods. Simulation results show that the proposed first-order varied-gain LTP obtains a speech quality that is near to that obtained with the fifth-order fixed gain LTP, however, the former requires much lower computation than the later.

articleTitle: Real-time display processing algorithms on a multimedia processor
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents software implementations of three display processing algorithms on a VLIW multimedia processor core. A combination of algorithm simplifications and software optimizations resulted in a real-time implementation for standard-definition video without compromising picture quality. Experimental results for deinterlacing, sharpness and color control algorithms are shown.

articleTitle: Presentation of ultrasonic environment by use of characteristics of digital sound
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In the reproduction of digitized sound, a method providing a more virtual and realistic environment is proposed by utilizing the ultrasonic component produced with sampling. Hearing tests show that this method is effective.

articleTitle: An efficient frame memory interface of MPEG-2 video encoder ASIC chip
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper an efficient frame memory interface of an MPEG-2 video encoder is presented. The proposed architecture takes about 58% less hardware area than the existing architecture (Kim et al. 1997), and results in reducing the total hardware area of the video encoder up to 24.3%.

articleTitle: Fully digital view-window control for intelligent video communication systems
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes a view-window control technique for intelligent video communication systems in which a local user can arbitrarily control the remote view-window and can magnify the selected area in the transmitted image without image degradation.

articleTitle: Edge-preserving directional regularization technique for disparity estimation of stereoscopic images
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper presents a new disparity estimation method using an edge-preserving directional regularization technique. This method smooths disparity vectors in smooth regions and preserves edges in object boundaries without oversmoothing. Very close matches between a left image and a right image are obtained as well as improved coding efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of turbo codes by error range search method in Rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We propose an efficient method of decoding turbo codes that can greatly reduce the iteration number with very low-complexity. The proposed ERS method reduces the number of iteration to obtain the required BER (bit error rate). Consequently, the number of iterations and latency required by the iterative decoding operation in turbo codes can be reduced and the interleaver's size can be minimized.

articleTitle: Wavelet image compression for mobile/portable applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Wavelet image compression offers several advantages over existing methods such as the DCT adopted in the JPEG standard, and has now been adopted by MPEG-4. This paper presents some wavelet codec implementation architectures obtained by a joint optimization of both the algorithmic and architectural features, according to system hardware and software strategy. Results are presented which allow optimization of system performance either for dedicated ASIC design or for embedded software implementation based on available execution speed and cache memory performance.

articleTitle: Block effect reduction with content-based AC prediction in an MPEG-2 compressed video
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper proposes a new block effect reduction technique, called content-based AC prediction, for an MPEG-2 compressed video. In the proposed algorithm, AC coefficients are predicted considering the image content itself in the DCT domain. Firstly, the algorithm detects which block has a block effect. Secondly, the algorithm finds whether the block is near the boundary of an image content or not. Then the adaptive AC prediction algorithm is applied to reduce the block effect.

articleTitle: High performance picture-in-picture (PIP) IC using embedded DRAM technology
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In the paper the next generation of a low cost, high performance single-chip picture-in-picture IC is presented. This chip will be produced in a 0.35 /spl mu/m eDRAM technology and integrates a digital multistandard color decoder, embedded DRAM, A/D and D/A converter and a data slicer for caption services. The paper deals with the digital video signal processing for color decoding with asynchronous sampling and the compensation of the skew. A new algorithm for a jointline-free true frame display is developed. The chip allows a smooth scaling from 1/81 to 1/4 of full screen picture size and implements a data compression algorithm for split-screen modes.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of speech coders for speech recognition in adverse communication environments
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We present the effect of several standard speech coders on speech recognition in adverse communication environments such as tandem, frame erasure, and noisy conditions. These environments were chosen to simulate the operational condition of IMT-2000. The comparative results can provide a guideline for selecting a speech coder when a speech recognition service is needed in digital communication networks.

articleTitle: Real-time DV transmission on hybrid network with IEEE 1394 and ATM
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes the hybrid network with IEEE 1394 and ATM (TCP/IP) for the home network, in which the real-time AV stream and control-command (AV/C) for DV-camcorder are transmitted.

articleTitle: Video rate control using activity based rate prediction
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient rate-prediction technique using the wavelet-based activity measure is proposed which can be successfully used for video rate-control. Experimental results show that the proposed prediction-based rate control scheme can regulate the bit-rate under dramatic scene changes more effectively and achieve better PSNR performance than the TM5 rate control mechanism.

articleTitle: Very low bit rate video codec using rearrangement of DCT coefficients and band-adaptive preprocessing
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel very low bit rate video codec using the wavelet restructure of DCT and band-adaptive preprocessing. The resulting design provides enhancements in coding efficiency, rate control precision, scalability, and error robustness.

articleTitle: Data broadcasting: what is the business? What is the market?
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Although there are technical issues in data broadcasting, much larger challenges lie in the development of successful business models. The conversion to digital television will create huge opportunities, but work needs to be done on enabling appropriate business models.

articleTitle: Construction of agent-oriented virtual society - PAW
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We constructed the agent-oriented virtual society (3D virtual multi-user world) PAW over the Internet. There are many autonomous agents acting with users in PAW. PAW was available on the Internet for about 6 months and gathered 30,000 registered users.

articleTitle: Development of 8 mm digital camcorder system
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have developed an 8 mm-digital camcorder system which allows users to record extremely high quality video and audio signals onto Hi8-MP 8mm tapes. We have also developed an automatic detector and high precision scanner for 8 mm-digital/analog8 so that this system has upper compatibility with the conventional analog 8mm VCR system.

articleTitle: A network MPEG camera
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: A network MPEG camera which can be directly connected to a network for real-time digital video transmission has been developed. The camera works under TCP/IP protocol, and accepts remote control commands from PCs. The command set of the camera includes record/pause command, mode change command, zoom control command, bit rate control command, and so on. The bit rate of MPEG video bit stream can be changed even in the data transmitting and encoding period.

articleTitle: An accurate bitrate control algorithm for MPEG-2 video coding
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: The MPEG-2 Test Model 5 (TM5) algorithm is widely used for bit rate control. In TM5, however, there are two well-known problems: scene change handling problem and non-uniform picture quality problem. This paper presents another problem that is a mismatching problem of the target number of bits and the number of actual coding bits for each picture. In this paper, we propose a new bitrate control algorithm for matching the target and actual coding bits, based on accurate bit estimation.

articleTitle: A design of VSB receiver IC for digital television
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: This paper describes a single ASIC chip that demodulates and decodes vestigial side band (VSB) digital TV signals. The VSB IC has been implemented for the receiver based on the ATSC digital TV standard. It can be applied to both modes of signal reception-8 VSB for terrestrial broadcast and 16 VSB for cable transmission.

articleTitle: DASE: the data applications software environment for DTV data broadcasting
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: Digital TV broadcast systems allow delivery of data and application programs to receivers, thus enabling interactive and data broadcast services. Such services must be delivered to consumers irrespective of the hardware and software platform of the receiver in the consumer's home. We discuss a software architecture for a DTV receiver that allows platform-independent content to be broadcast for service provision.

articleTitle: On video formats and coding efficiency
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We have studied the effectiveness of MPEG-2 coding for interlaced and progressive video, and compared deinterlacing and picture-rate up-conversion before and after coding. We found receiver side processing to be superior.

articleTitle: Implementation of noise reduction IC using a recursive temporal filter with motion detection
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: We describe a practical implementation of a recursive noise reduction filter which employs an adaptive temporal filtering algorithm with motion detection and can minimize a variant of artifacts occurring in digital image sequences.

articleTitle: DCT-based high resolution digital zooming algorithm
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a digital zooming algorithm to reconstruct a high-resolution image from multiple aliased low resolution images, which is based on the generalized deconvolution technique. The conventional approaches are based on the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) since the aliasing effect is easily analyzed in the frequency domain. However, the useful solution may not be available in many cases, i.e., the underdetermined cases or the insufficient subpixel information cases. In order to compensate for such ill-posedness, the generalized regularization was adopted in the spatial domain. Furthermore, the use of the discrete cosine transform (DCT) instead of the DFT leads to the computationally efficient reconstruction algorithm. The validity of the proposed algorithm is both theoretically and experimentally demonstrated in this paper. It is also shown that the artifact caused by inaccurate motion information is reduced by regularization.

articleTitle: Very high throughput crypto-system architectures: the RPK solution
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
abstract: RPK is a new cryptographic algorithm based on the discrete logarithm problem implemented using discrete exponentiation over finite Galois fields GF[2/sup n/]. This paper presents a high throughput RPK architecture, suitable for encrypting high bit-rate multimedia contents.

articleTitle: System considerations on SCPC for digital satellite receivers with direct conversion
publicationTitle: 1999 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (Cat. No.99CH36277)
